key_insight: All tested URANS models capture start-up torque, mass flow, and leading-edge blade-passing frequency content, but RSM better resolves trailing-edge and draft-tube frequency content.
engineering_relevance: Computationally tractable start-up simulations can support variable-speed pump-turbine design by characterizing transients relevant to fatigue loading.
method: Simulate a linear start-up of a variable-speed reversible pump-turbine using transient CFD.
Compare k–ω SST, EARSM, and RSM turbulence models within a URANS framework.
Evaluate torque, mass flow, and local frequency content.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports accurate global quantities across all models and better downstream frequency resolution with RSM, attributed to its consistent representation of turbulence anisotropy.
watch_item: The abstract gives no quantitative errors or runtime costs, so accuracy and computational feasibility should be verified for the intended design workflow.
paper_title: Transient CFD simulation of a linear start-up of a variable speed reversible pump-turbine
